def: A piece of code produced by a search loop whose quality is not yet known and which must be tested before it is trusted.
An evaluator that maps every outcome, including crashes, hangs and garbage output, to a score, so the search never receives an exception.
A limit on how long a parent waits for a child before it gives up and kills it.
A cap on CPU time, memory or file size that the operating system enforces on a process.
A resource limit on the seconds of processor work a process may use, which a sleeping process never reaches.
A fixed set of workers that take jobs from a queue, so many tasks can run at once without starting a worker for each.
A lock in standard CPython that lets only one thread run Python bytecode at a time, so threads do not speed up CPU-bound work.
A placeholder for a result that a worker will produce later; waiting on it with a timeout does not stop the worker.
A seed computed from a parent seed and an index, usually by hashing, so each candidate gets its own repeatable random stream.
A fixed-size fingerprint computed from the bytes of some content, used as a cache key because equal content gives an equal hash.
One standard text for a program, made by parsing it and printing it back, so formatting and comments do not change its identity.
A file where new records are only added at the end and old ones never change, so a crash can damage only the last record.
A text format with one JSON object per line, easy to append to and to replay line by line.
